title.narrative: Support to People Affected by Super Typhoon Man-yi and Recent Typhoons

description.narrative: On 13 November 2024, the CERF Anticipatory Action (AA) readiness trigger for the Bicol Region (Scenario 1) was activated in anticipation of the onslaught of Super Typhoon Pepito (international name: Man-Yi). Despite the typhoon forecast of i) sustained winds of 85 km/h, ii) a forward movement of 25 km/h, iii) an estimated 8,000 totally damaged houses, and iv) a 67 percent probability of impact, the conditions fell below the required 85 percent probability threshold for activating CERF AA within the 72-hour period. Super Typhoon Pepito intensified to Category 5 as it made its first landfall in Catanduanes, one of the areas covered under the CERF AA Scenario 1. The typhoon caused severe damage to agriculture and community infrastructure. In response, the CERF AA UN implementing agencies appealed to transition AA funds into a rapid response mechanism. This appeal was approved, enabling redeployment of funds for emergency response operation. Under the emergency response, WFP will provide i) cash assistance and community cash grants to heavily affected areas which are also under WFP’s CERF AA geographic priority in Catanduanes (Region 5), and ii) cash assistance in Aurora (Region 2) and Cagayan (Region 3) which were affected by the other five consecutive typhoons since late October. WFP will work with the national government through the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) and local governments in delivering the assistance. WFP aims to reach a total of 14,905 households in Aurora, Cagayan, Catanduanes, and other severely affected areas in Bicol Region with cash assistance. WFP will provide cash assistance worth US$115 (PHP 6,700) for each household. This amount is comprised of the CERF AA-approved transfer value of US$56 (PHP 3,300) and an additional US$0.86 (PHP 50) per month for two months to cover the beneficiary’s transportation cost. In Catanduanes, WFP will refer to its CERF AA Standard Operating Procedures in the transition to rapid response. The cash transfer is designed to meet immediate food and other basic needs and support early recovery. Cash distributions will be done through cooperating partners and Western Union (WU), utilizing MTCN codes redeemable at WU local branches and affiliates or mobile wallets. In areas with reliable network connectivity, WFP will send MTCN codes to beneficiaries’ mobile numbers using the WFP SCOPE platform. For areas with limited network coverage but with access to WU outlets, WFP will work with cooperating partners to print and distribute MTCN codes onsite. In geographically isolated areas, cash will be distributed directly to beneficiaries through cooperating partners. For beneficiaries identified as DSWD’s 4Ps (Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program) members, WFP will transfer cash assistance directly to their bank accounts via the WFP PlugPay system. To support the rehabilitation of critical community assets, WFP will provide community cash grants up to US$10,000 each to at least three community organizations in the most affected areas as identified by the authorities and communities. The grant amount will be determined based on estimated budget required for rebuilding essential livelihood assets and small-scale community infrastructure, employing a community-driven approach.WFP will closely work with partner local governments including conduct of joint assessments with the Humanitarian Country Team (HCT) and other government agencies. In the context of reprogramming AA into rapid response, sensitization of beneficiaries and government officials plays a critical role to ensure a common understanding and expectations from the programme. WFP will cascade information about the response and recovery objectives, key components, and distribution processes. Post-distribution monitoring will also be conducted. At the conclusion of the response, WFP will hand over the activities to the local government and facilitate an After-Action Review to inform future interventions.
